status: EXAMPLE CONTENT written by the student team in plain English. A nurse or clinical lead must review it before any real use.

notes.title: Hydration
lines: A resident who is not drinking enough may have a dry mouth, dark urine, be more sleepy or confused than usual, or keep refusing drinks.
Offer a drink often and with every meal. Keep a drink within reach and record how much is taken.
Tell the nurse if a resident keeps refusing drinks.

notes.title: Falls
lines: A resident may be at higher risk of falling if they are unsteady when standing, feel dizzy, are newly confused, or have had a recent near-fall.
Keep the walking frame within reach, keep floors clear, and stay close when the resident stands or walks.
Report any fall or near-fall to the nurse on shift straight away.

notes.title: Poor appetite and vomiting
lines: Signs to watch for include leaving most of a meal, saying they feel sick, vomiting, or looking pale and weak.
Offer small, light meals and sips of fluid often. Write down the time and roughly how much was vomited.
Tell the nurse if a resident vomits or cannot keep fluids down.

notes.title: Skin and pressure areas
lines: Signs of skin trouble include red or sore skin that does not fade, a new blister, or a resident saying an area is sore.
Help the resident change position regularly, and keep skin clean and dry.
Tell the nurse about any change in the skin.
